clusters.name: Jonah's move to the conservatory, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around his start at Wexley Conservatory in September 1991, within months: a wrist injury that stopped his playing and left him anxious and unable to function, a blow-up with his close friend Rafe who moved out, retreat into his room getting high and absorbed in radios, and a fall into feeling lost and low. His grandfather Gordon died in June 1991, and his mother remarried that autumn; with his grandfather gone and his footing gone, he had no stability. By spring 1992 he was earning money fixing radios and had some traction, though the bleak year at community college followed.

clusters.name: Desmond's move to Quarry Lane and the household rebuild, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around April 1989 when Desmond took a rental on Quarry Lane while the Hollin Road house was rebuilt, within the years that follow: Jonah's late nights started that autumn and grew through his teens, he settled in the rebuilt house that fall with his mother and Desmond and Desmond's two children, loud and cramped, his mother filled in his college forms without his say, and in early 1994 he was stung that his father had never heard of the film he was making. His grandfather Clifford returned to the family around the same time the move began. The shifts in these years are Jonah's own, and no one else's shows then.

clusters.name: Jonah's burnout and the failed audition, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around September 2001 when Jonah's performing began to lose its hold and his anxiety rose, within the months and years that follow: his grandmother Winifred was found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, a disastrous audition for the national orchestra in early 2002 ended his performer's life, he fell into distance on poor terms with family and friends, left Thornbury for Gull Harbour and then met Marisol, moved to Fenwick with her by mid-2003, split from her that October and sank into a deep depression, returned to Thornbury and could not face his family, relied on friends Corbin, Dale, and Hamish instead. His grandmother spent her final months in his parents' home in autumn 2003 and died in February 2004. The period settles as he began swimming, returned to his therapist Victor Halloran, and requested his parents' help with therapy costs in January 2004.

clusters.name: Lorna's death and Jonah's cutoff from his mother, 2008
clusters.reason: Around January 2008 when his grandmother Lorna died, within months: Jonah spent four weeks building with Silas at Alder Creek before nursing school, was too drained for conversation with his mother there, she pressed him to visit when the timing was wrong and the visit went badly with the door shut against her, and when he left for nursing school at Marlow Sound in August 2008 he stopped speaking to her, a silence that held for roughly a year. His other grandmother Winifred had died four years before; the cluster of deaths in his extended family sits with his move and the cutoff. The events before the silence show the gathering strain; the silence itself marks where he settled into distance.

clusters.name: Wren's family gathering and Jonah's sleep crisis, 2019–2020
clusters.reason: Around October 2019 when Wren's mother Frances retired and the family gathered at the lake house, within days: Wren was swamped with events one after another and her symptom and anxiety rose, her functioning fell, Jonah overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her, Wren's close fusion with her father Hugo and brother Leo meant every bit of news traveled between them, she settled once the weekend had a plan and the dinner went well, but Jonah awoke from the small hours at the lake with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose, his symptom and anxiety spiked and he kept his distance, and Wren became anxious when he'd had no sleep at family occasions with long quiet drives home afterward. Jonah's marriage to Wren in March 2017 had begun a slight easing of his contact with his mother; the lake weekend brought his sleep difficulties into sharp focus within Wren's family.

periods.name: the year he left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
